far_updates.title: Comments closed on the second batch of FAR Overhaul proposed rules
far_updates.body: The FAR Council's second set of four proposed rules, published 18 September 2026, covered about 16 more FAR parts. Four more proposed rules and then the final rules are still to come. Until then, DoW keeps using its RFO class deviations.
far_updates.details: The public had until 19 October 2026 to comment on the four September proposed rules. The FAR Council (the group that writes the FAR) now reviews those comments before it writes the final rules. Its notices say the overhaul has twelve proposed rules in all, so four are still to come; none had been published by 18 November 2026. Four parts on the exam's list of 20 are not in any proposed rule yet: Parts 19, 31, 42 and 46. Until final rules take effect, DoW keeps using its RFO class deviations, and that RFO text is what the exam tests. WarU has said it will adjust the exam, and announce when, if rulemaking changes what the exam covers.

far_updates.title: CON 7300V Price Analysis is now required for certification
far_updates.body: For the DoW Contracting Professional certification, CON 7300V must be completed after CON 1300V. Components decide whether it applies to people already working on their certification; DoW expects them to take it. Already certified? It is encouraged, not required.
far_updates.source: DPCAP memo, Contracting Functional Area Certification Change for FY27 (5 Jun 2026)
far_updates.details: A DPCAP memo signed 5 June 2026 made CON 7300V part of the DoW Contracting Professional certification from 1 October 2026. DoW's analysis of exam results showed that pricing is the skill where the workforce can improve the most, and CON 1300V does not teach it in enough depth. The course is 28 hours over 7 days, all virtual: mostly self-paced for three days, then instructor-led days that end with a graded price analysis simulation. WarU suggests an Excel course first if Excel is new to you. Since 1 October 2026, people still working toward their certification get first priority for seats. Ask your Contracting Master Gunner (KMG) early whether the rule applies to you and when to request a seat.

far_updates.title: New certification exam FAQs
far_updates.body: FY26 average score was 74.8% and 79% passed on the first try. Test centers pass about 4% more than online testing. Answers come from the RFO-updated FAR and DFARS. Up to three attempts in 12 months, at least 30 days apart.
far_updates.source: DoW Contracting Professional Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)
far_updates.details:
DPCAP's exam FAQ dated 1 October 2026 is the newest official word on CON 3990V; the app's Official documents page has a copy. Besides the FY26 results, it confirms these points:
- 150 multiple-choice questions and 3 hours of seat time (the tutorial and breaks count), closed book, 70% to pass.
- DoW recommends a Pearson test center; use online testing (OnVUE) only by exception.
- Reschedule at least 48 hours ahead. Cancelling without a new date uses one of your three tries.
- If your first try fails, take CON 3900V before the next one (unless you took it before; CON 3910 is its prerequisite).
- Know the titles of the 20 FAR parts it lists, and read FAR Part 15 closely: many questions come from it.

far_updates.title: Second batch of FAR Overhaul proposed rules
far_updates.body: Four more proposed rules continued the formal rulemaking phase of the overhaul.
far_updates.details: On 18 September 2026 the FAR Council (the group that writes the FAR) published four more proposed rules in the Federal Register. Together they cover Parts 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 27, 28, 35, 36, 38, 44, 47 and 51, plus more clause changes in Part 52. Six of these are on the exam's list of 20 FAR parts: 8, 12, 13, 15, 16 and 44. A proposed rule is a draft for public comment; it is not in effect yet, so keep studying the RFO text DoW uses now. GSA also made a related proposal on 22 September 2026. It would move the Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) ordering steps out of the FAR and into GSA's own rules (GSAR part 538).

far_updates.title: DoW certified cost or pricing data threshold is now $10 million
far_updates.body: For DoW prime contracts awarded after 30 June 2026, certified cost or pricing data are required above $10 million unless an exception applies (FY2026 NDAA; DFARS 215.403-3 class deviation). The governmentwide FAR figure is still $2.5 million.
far_updates.source: 10 U.S.C. 3702; DoW Class Deviation for DFARS Part 215
far_updates.details:
The FY2026 NDAA changed the law (10 U.S.C. 3702), and DoW put the new figure into DFARS 215.403-3(a) through its Part 215 class deviation. For DoW, the award date decides the line: after 30 June 2026 it is $10 million; on or before that date it stays $2.5 million unless the contract says otherwise. FAR 15.403-2 still forbids asking for certified cost or pricing data in these cases:
- at or below the SAT
- adequate price competition
- prices set by law or regulation
- commercial products and commercial services (also when modifying a contract for them)
- a waiver from the head of the contracting activity (HCA)

far_updates.title: Formal rulemaking for the FAR Overhaul begins
far_updates.body: The first four proposed rules covered Parts 1 to 7, 10, 33, 49 and others. Formal rules will eventually replace the class deviations agencies use today.
far_updates.details: On 23 June 2026 the FAR Council (the group that writes the FAR) published the first four proposed rules of the overhaul. They appeared in the Federal Register, where the Government publishes new rules, and comments were due by 23 July 2026. They cover Parts 1 to 7, 10, 18, 24, 26, 29, 33, 37, 39, 40, 41, 49 and 53, plus clause changes in Part 52. OMB, the White House budget office, called this the first of three releases; the notices say twelve proposed rules in all. A proposed rule is a draft and is not in effect, so DoW contracting officers keep using the RFO class deviations. Ten of these parts are on the exam's list of 20 (1 to 7, 10, 33 and 49), so learn their RFO numbers and titles well.

far_updates.title: CON 1400V updated for the FAR Overhaul
far_updates.body: Classes starting on or after 11 May 2026 teach the RFO-updated post-award rules.
far_updates.details: WarU's catalog page for CON 1400V says the course now matches the RFO, and everyone enrolled from 11 May 2026 gets the new content. It is still 5 class days, virtual, and needs only CON 1100 or 1100V first, so you can take it while you wait for a CON 1300V seat. WarU's student FAQ of 16 April 2026 says the core learning goals of the certification courses did not change much; the examples and terms changed to match the RFO. If you took CON 1400V before 11 May 2026, check your notes against the RFO numbers (FAR & key numbers, Old → new numbers). Also, until RFO rulemaking ends, CON 1100 runs 4 full days instead of 8.

far_updates.title: CON 3990V now tests the RFO FAR
far_updates.body: The updated certification exam went live on 31 March 2026 (the last legacy exam was 30 March). About 30% of the question bank changed; the competencies did not. Study materials that use pre-RFO numbers, like many class slides, need checking: see Exam path, Class material check.
far_updates.source: WarU, How the RFO Will Affect CON Certification: Student FAQ Sheet (16 Apr 2026)
far_updates.details: WarU switched the exam to its RFO version all at once, so every exam from 31 March 2026 uses it. Its student FAQ of 16 April 2026 says the RFO did not change the DoW contracting competencies in substance. So the exam still tests the same skills, at the initial readiness level. It also says the recent dollar threshold changes did not change any question or answer, because of how the questions are written. The prep courses CON 3910 and CON 3900V were updated by 1 March 2026. Before you trust a deck, slide or practice test, check its date: anything made before 31 March 2026 may teach old FAR numbers.

far_updates.title: FPDS.gov retired; award reporting is in SAM.gov
far_updates.body: Contract award data is now reported and searched in SAM.gov.
far_updates.details: On 24 February 2026, GSA finished moving FPDS.gov's public functions into SAM.gov and shut down ezSearch, the old FPDS search tool. All contract award data that was in FPDS.gov is now in SAM.gov, and old FPDS.gov links go to SAM.gov. Anyone with a SAM.gov account can search it; you must sign in, but no special role is needed. Contract writing systems still send award data, now through SAM.gov's contract awards portal (sam.gov/contracting for federal users). Older slides and guides that say FPDS mean this data: look for it in SAM.gov, for example when you research past awards and prices.

far_updates.title: DoW adopts the FAR Overhaul
far_updates.body: DoW's RFO class deviations, with matching DFARS changes, took effect. Many FAR sections were renumbered: for example, sole-source authority moved from 6.302-1 to 6.103-1 and ratification from 1.602-3 to 1.405.
far_updates.details: A DPCAP memo signed 19 December 2025 announced DoW's first 31 RFO class deviations, effective 1 February 2026; the last ones came in early March 2026. The deviations tell contracting officers to use the RFO text of each FAR part on acquisition.gov, plus a revised DFARS part and PGI. That text replaces the old text in the Code of Federal Regulations. DoW kept the DFARS rules that law requires or sound buying needs; most other policies were removed, rewritten or moved to the PGI. DPCAP has revised many deviations since, several between July and October 2026, so always use the current version on DPCAP's class deviation page. Old templates and slides still show pre-RFO numbers: match them to the new ones with the app's Old → new numbers list.

far_updates.title: FY2026 NDAA signed
far_updates.body: Among many acquisition changes, it raised DoW's certified cost or pricing data threshold (for awards after 30 June 2026) and DoW's justification approval levels ($10 million contracting officer, $100 million competition advocate, $500 million head of the contracting activity).
far_updates.details:
The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2026 became law on 18 December 2025 as Public Law 119-60. DoW put its new figures into its DFARS class deviations; the governmentwide FAR figures are lower, so always check whether DoW's DFARS or the FAR applies. Section 1804 changed two sets of numbers you will use:
- Certified cost or pricing data: above $10 million for DoW prime contracts entered into after 30 June 2026 (DFARS 215.403-3).
- Justification and approval (J&A): contracting officer up to $10 million; competition advocate over $10 million to $100 million; head of the contracting activity over $100 million to $500 million; senior procurement executive over $500 million (DFARS Table 206-1).

far_updates.title: DAU becomes the Warfighting Acquisition University (WarU)
far_updates.body: The school that teaches the certification courses and owns the exam was renamed as part of DoW's acquisition transformation. Its catalog moved to icatalog.waru.edu.
far_updates.details: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced the change in a speech on 7 November 2025. He said the school would become a competency-based institution that teaches through projects on real problems and case studies. It is the same school: it still teaches the certification courses (CON 1100V, 1200V, 1300V, 1400V and 7300V) and runs the CON 3990V exam. Its catalog is at icatalog.waru.edu, and old dau.edu links open on waru.edu. Older certificates, transcripts and slides, and even some laws, still say DAU; they mean the same school.

far_updates.title: Inflation adjustment raises key thresholds
far_updates.body: Micro-purchase threshold $15,000 (from $10,000), simplified acquisition threshold $350,000 (from $250,000), FAR certified cost or pricing data threshold $2.5 million, and commercial simplified procedures $9 million.
far_updates.details:
This five-year inflation update (FAR Case 2024-001) came out in Federal Acquisition Circular 2025-06 on 27 August 2025 and took effect on 1 October 2025. For DoW awards after 30 June 2026, the certified cost or pricing data line is now $10 million instead of $2.5 million. The same update also raised these figures, which older flashcard decks and guides still show at their old values:
- Contingency micro-purchase threshold: $25,000 inside the U.S. and $40,000 outside.
- Contingency SAT: $1 million inside the U.S. and $2 million outside.
- Small business subcontracting plans: over $900,000 ($2 million for construction).

far_updates.title: The Revolutionary FAR Overhaul begins
far_updates.body: Executive Order 14275 said the FAR should keep only what the law requires or what sound buying needs. OFPP and the FAR Council answered with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul, a plain-language rewrite.
far_updates.details: The President signed Executive Order 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement, on 15 April 2025. It says the FAR should keep only rules that a law requires or that are essential to sound buying, and remove the rest. It gave the head of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP) 180 days to start amending the FAR. OFPP does this work with the FAR Council (the group that writes the FAR) and the agencies. They named the work the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO): a part-by-part rewrite in plain language, with model text for the parts released from 28 May to 7 November 2025. That is why the FAR you study has new section numbers and shorter text.

guide_changes.title: What the field test found
guide_changes.notes: Most lessons now end with a short game on that lesson's own questions or words. On a phone that cannot draw 3D, Range Day's campaign and range-card missions play as Qual Range, the same drill in 2D, so no month is blocked; a locked month says what opens it, and the Arcade explains itself in three steps. Read-aloud stops when you move on and says "dash" in citations, and while a picture plays, the part being read pops. FAR links open at the cited section and paragraph, U.S. Code links open the right section, and each item under What changed lately opens to the whole story. Also: KO instead of CO in the games, PD2 removed, VCE-PCF, a Guiding Principles bay in Dispatch, and the intro shows the read-aloud.

guide_changes.title: Ready for everyone
guide_changes.notes: The website now opens on a two-minute intro video the first time (muted, with its words under it; tap Sound on, or Skip). Watch it again from About or Settings & help. The QR code always lands on the install page, with one Install app button on any Android browser. Certification 101 adds what the 51C proponent said about CON 7300V, the degree and the next reclassification window, and a new question on full CON 7300V classes. Plus fixes from the release check: the terms of use, the phone's top-bar colour, Buddy, the tour and six practice questions; and in the Arcade, long sessions of 3D games no longer slow the phone down, and results count the range card's XP.

guide_changes.title: The range card, the qualification table and the seasons
guide_changes.notes: Three five-minute missions a day on a range card, with a streak you can repair once a week; a weekly 40-target qualification table scored like the Army rifle standard (23 Marksman, 30 Sharpshooter, 36 Expert) that every answer in any game fires; and fiscal-year seasons with range skins for Range Day and Fire Mission (Desert, Korea winter, Forest, High summer). Home shows the card and the badge.

guide_changes.title: The 3D games on a phone
guide_changes.notes: A 3D game no longer sits on a blank screen while it loads on a phone: it opens on a loading card and starts when its first frame is ready. The games test the phone's graphics once and pick simpler drawing when needed, hold a steady frame rate by drawing smaller, and say so and offer Restart if the phone stops the 3D view. Under the game list, "Check this phone" runs a 3D test whose result you can send to the developer.

guide_changes.title: Fixes from the first tester
guide_changes.notes: Hear a sample and Listen work better on iPhones: novelty voices such as Bells are gone from the list, and a voice that does not start now says what to check. Range Day keeps all three targets on screen on an upright phone. The range games ask only exam words, not training and career terms, and DAU shows as WarU's old name.

guide_changes.title: What the 51C proponent said
guide_changes.notes: Four new questions in Certification 101 from an October 2026 session with the 51C proponent, checked against USAASC's pages: who the proponent is and how to reach them, how a Soldier becomes a 51C, where the promotion-board guidance is, and what to weigh before a job off the 51C path. The proponent's page also confirms that AATC gives the WarU course equivalencies. Three new Career links and four glossary terms.

guide_changes.title: Fire Mission no longer starts black
guide_changes.notes: The 3D valley showed a black picture until the first round was fired; the muzzle-flash light started with an invalid intensity. Fixed.

guide_changes.title: Five games in real 3D and the whole first year
guide_changes.notes: Fire Mission (an M777 across a valley, trucks that burn), Part Patrol (a fighter over a planet, the Dreadnought with real turrets) and Dispatch, the sorting yard that was Sort Yard, are now drawn in real 3D like Range Day and Supply Line. The campaign is complete: chapters 5 to 12 cover the review, exam week and the first year on the job, three missions each across every game.

guide_changes.title: Onboarding with a voice and a theme
guide_changes.notes: The first visit is a four-step setup: who you are, your dates, how it looks (day or night, six colour themes, text size) and read-aloud (pick a voice, hear a sample). Themes are also in Settings & help → Display and in the side menu's Theme button; each has a day and a night look.

guide_changes.title: Range Day boards keep their distance
guide_changes.notes: The three target boards no longer touch or overlap on screen: the lanes widen with each row's distance, and the first level draws its boards at 25 and 50 metres only.

guide_changes.title: Text size in one place
guide_changes.notes: The side menu's bottom panel now shows Day / night only. Text size is set under Settings & help, Display tab; on a wide screen the Aa button at the top still cycles it.

guide_changes.title: Supply Line in real 3D, four bosses, the Master Gunner and the campaign
guide_changes.notes: Supply Line's convoy is now drawn in real 3D, from dawn at the Ops Center to night at the FOB, with the five checkpoints as real places. Contract Quest's bosses are the Unauthorized Commitment, the Bid Bust, the Audit and the Protest, each with its own questions and a second-phase attack. Your Master Gunner briefs and reacts in a bubble. The campaign, Your first year as a 51C, opens with chapters 1 to 4: three missions each across Range Day, Supply Line and a boss fight.

guide_changes.title: Terms and privacy on their own pages
guide_changes.notes: The terms of use and a plain privacy page (no tracking; what an account stores, with or without Google; how to delete it) now have their own pages on the website, linked from About, so you can read or share them without opening the app.

guide_changes.title: Eleven more questions, a cite fixed, bigger buttons on phones
guide_changes.notes: The contingency, systems and exam lessons gained eleven questions. Lesson 33 now cites DFARS 225.371-3 and clause 252.225-7040 for SPOT. Buddy answers questions about voices. Cite chips, lesson Play buttons, glossary letters and the top-bar buttons are easier to tap on a phone.

guide_changes.title: Range Day: the rifle range in real 3D
guide_changes.notes: A new Arcade game drawn in real 3D: the tower reads a glossary clue, three targets pop up with terms, and you fire an M4A1 at the right one. Twenty exposures and thirty rounds, scored Expert, Sharpshooter or Marksman like a rifle table. Real light and shadows, bloom, brass, splinters and bullet holes. Qual Range, the 2D version, stays.

guide_changes.title: App voices: a man or a woman, US or UK, the same on every phone
guide_changes.notes: Settings & help → Display → Read aloud → Voice now offers four App voices (Amber, Joe, Cori, Leo). Each is a one-time download of about 63 MB (plus 31 MB for the speech engine the first time) and then works offline. On Android the phone's own voice list could not change the voice; these can.

guide_changes.title: Terms of use: Google sign-in spelled out
guide_changes.notes: The terms now say you can create your account with Google and what Google passes on (your name, email address and profile picture link); nothing else is collected. Because the terms changed, the app asks you to agree once more. Continue with Google while offline now tells you to connect first.

guide_changes.title: What the owner confirmed about the Army process
guide_changes.notes: The local goal is 6 months in most contracting support brigades; a system role takes two to three weeks; MICC's onboarding is NGAP; the certification request goes through CAMP by authorized personnel; a missed 36-month deadline is usually covered by an exception to policy.

guide_changes.title: Continue with Google
guide_changes.notes: The Sign in pop-up now starts with a Continue with Google button: one tap with your Google account, no password to make up or remember, and your progress saves to the account the same way. Email and password still work, and the app says hello by the name on your Google account.

guide_changes.title: Every lesson and question checked against the FAR Overhaul
guide_changes.notes: All 35 lessons and 384 questions were read against the RFO text on acquisition.gov, cite by cite. Thirteen corrections, the biggest in Lesson 1: the guiding principles are now the seven RFO principles in FAR 1.102(a). Also fixed: the QASP cite (DFARS 237.172), f.o.b. and risk-of-loss cites, sources sought and RFI cites, the competitive range wording, and a credential code. Seven glossary terms added. A lesson's Check yourself now shows up to six questions with a button for the rest, and the Practice test takes keyboard shortcuts (1 to 4, Enter, arrows, F).

guide_changes.title: Read-aloud with rise and fall
guide_changes.notes: Listen buttons now read the way a person does: questions rise, sentences settle, headings get a breath, lists keep a beat. Settings & help → Display → Read aloud has a Tone switch (Lively or Even) beside the voice and speed. FAR cites, Part IV, plurals and twenty more contracting words are said the way people say them. Buddy's bubble draws itself from a dot and gives a gentle, regular nudge until you open it once.

guide_changes.title: Pick a voice that sounds like a person
guide_changes.notes: Settings & help → Read aloud lists the voices on your phone or computer, natural ones first, with a sample and a speed slider, and tells you how to download a more human voice. Listen buttons now say acronyms and course numbers the way contracting people say them.

guide_changes.title: Meet Buddy, your study buddy
guide_changes.notes: Tap the chat bubble on any page and ask in plain words: what is a KO, how much is the SAT, how do I register in AITAS. Buddy answers from the guide on your device, with no internet and no AI account, and opens the page to read more. Need more depth? One tap sends your question to Google AI Mode, ChatGPT or Claude in your own account. Home has a new look, and pages now rise into view as you scroll.

guide_changes.title: One install button, and accounts with your name
guide_changes.notes: Open the website on a phone and you get the app's install page with one button for your phone: Install app in Chrome on Android, Install with Chrome in Samsung Internet (which otherwise shows an unsafe-app warning), or the three Safari taps on an iPhone. Sign in now sits in the top bar; creating an account asks for your name, can show your password while you type it, and the app says hello by name.

guide_changes.title: Save your progress to an account
guide_changes.notes: Optional: under Settings & help → Your account, create an account with your email and a password. Your progress saves to it after every change and comes back on any phone or computer where you sign in.

guide_changes.title: B2B Guide is now B2B Exam Prep
guide_changes.notes: New name, same app: B2B Exam Prep (B2B Prep on your home screen). Opening it in a browser now asks you to install the app first, with one tap on Android or three Safari steps on iPhone. Your progress carries over.

guide_changes.title: What to trust from outside the guide
guide_changes.notes: The exam page (Certification, The exam) now has Study material from other places: what to use first (CON 3910, the exam FAQ, the FAR Companion, the whole RFO in one PDF, FAI's FAR Overhaul training and Pearson's demo test), how to check a Quizlet deck or free site before you trust it, and why to skip anything sold as the real exam. Most free decks online were made before the exam moved to the overhauled FAR on 31 March 2026. Ten new practice questions cover the exam areas the bank had few questions on: Skills and Roles, Situational Assessment, Team Dynamics, the seller's Plan Sales and Prepare Offer, and Plan Negotiations. Links has five new official links.

guide_changes.title: Install the app in one tap
guide_changes.notes: Opened B2B Guide in a phone browser? A Get the app card now installs it on Android with one tap, and shows iPhone users the three Safari steps. Once installed it opens full screen from its own icon and keeps your progress.

guide_changes.title: B2B Guide is now a phone app
guide_changes.notes: Scan the QR code (About page, or the printed install sheet) to install B2B Guide on an iPhone or Android phone: free, no app store, no account. It works offline after the first open, and new versions arrive by themselves. B2B Guide now opens with short terms of use: it is owned by SFC Rabin Napit, free for your own study and for sharing unchanged, but not to copy, change or sell.

guide_changes.title: Lesson pictures and a fairer question bank
guide_changes.notes: Every lesson now opens with pictures you can play (each part lights up and is read aloud) and, for the dollar rules, Try it tools that answer for any amount: who does what, the dollar ladder, the contract-type risk scale, the debriefing and protest clocks, closeout times and more, in icons and short words. The practice questions were rebalanced so the right answer is no longer usually the longest option, so practice scores now show real readiness. The guided tour now opens every main page, including Official documents. The AITAS links now open the AITAS landing page, where you register for courses.

guide_changes.title: Official documents, picture explanations and Supply Line
guide_changes.notes: New Arcade game, Supply Line: lead a supply convoy to the FOB through five checkpoints, one for each part of the contract life cycle; right answers load the cargo and clean runs earn challenge coins. New Official documents page: 26 DoW and WarU documents behind the certification, each with a simple picture version and the real pages (the exam FAQ, roadmap, flowchart, CON 7300V memo, career model, competency model and more open inside the file, without internet). Certification 101 now explains the exam with pictures: the exam journey step by step, the 48-hour and 90-day rules, retakes, the 36-month clock, continuous learning points and your career path. New study tips from the WarU exam team, updated credential codes, and continuous learning that starts when you join, not when you certify.

guide_changes.title: Guided tour, About page and day mode
guide_changes.notes: A guided tour shows what each part of the guide is for (offered on first open; the ? button or the ? key starts it again). New About page with the developer and maintainer and a feedback button. The side menu collapses to a rail of icons. Day mode is now the default (Settings & help can follow your device instead). Top bar labels no longer run off the top of the window. In Contract Quest a right answer now fires your RPG.

guide_changes.title: The B2B Arcade
guide_changes.notes: Practice → Arcade: five action games on the guide's own content. Contract Quest (RPG battles through the four exam areas), Fire Mission (artillery on thresholds, deadlines and forms), Qual Range (pop-up targets for glossary terms, scored Expert to Marksman), Part Patrol (a space shooter on FAR parts, UCF sections and PIID letters) and Sort Yard (a conveyor sorting line). Four paces, XP and ranks, and a study list after every run. The exam path has nine Arcade tasks; the old games are now Quick drills.

guide_changes.title: 6-Month Exam Path and the B2B class materials
guide_changes.notes: New Exam path: 26 dated weeks with tasks, weekly checks and monthly timed checkpoints. The Back to Basics class materials were checked against the RFO FAR: 143 class practice questions added (91 still right, 38 updated, 14 corrected), 34 questions on topics past test takers reported, 52 class claims checked, 31 test-taker topics, and four new flashcard decks (Jeopardy review, UCF, forms, PIID letters). Fixed a lesson that still listed the reserved 52.212-5.

guide_changes.title: First test version
guide_changes.notes: Plan builder, Certification 101, 19 courses, 35 lessons, 197 practice questions with an exam simulator, flashcards, four games, a glossary of about 245 terms and a FAR reference. Built for testing with new 51Cs and 1102s.
